newsitem.title: USA: Congressman behind Lebed trip to Clinton inaugural.
newsitem.headline: Congressman behind Lebed trip to Clinton inaugural.

text.p: A Republican senator was behind the mysterious invitation to retired Russian general Alexander Lebed to President Bill Clinton's inaugural swearing-in ceremony next Monday, a member of the senator's staff said.
A spokeswoman for Delaware Sen. William Roth said Roth provided three tickets to a constituent in his state who requested them with the express purpose of inviting Lebed to the festivities.
The tough-talking Lebed, who sees himself as a potential successor to Russian President Boris Yeltsin, insisted this week he was invited to attend the ceremonies by Clinton.
But the White House, which strongly supported Yeltsin, denied it. White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday: "I don't know how he got a ticket. He was not invited by the United States."
McCurry suggested Lebed was a guest of the Joint Inaugural Committee, made up of leaders of Congress, but a spokesman denied that, deepening the mystery.

Roth's spokeswoman stressed the initiative for the invitation came from the Delaware constituent, who she declined to name. All 535 members of Congress are allotted tickets for the inaugural ceremony.
But she said Roth, chairman of the North Atlantic Assembly, NATO's parliamentary forum, would meet Lebed on Monday to discuss NATO expansion.
Lebed opposes NATO expansion into East European countries that were previously members of the Soviet bloc but Roth strongly favours the policy.
The spokeswoman said Roth made available three invitations to the swearing-in ceremony on the front steps of the Capitol.

Lebed, who will be accompanied by his wife, Inna, was expecte to arrive in Washington on Sunday and travel to Wilmington, Delaware, and New York before leaving on Thursday, according to a New York travel agency arranging his trip.
